title: The Chameleon’s Limit: Investigating Persona Collapse and Homogenization in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the proportion of behavioral variance (via eta-squared and incremental R-squared) in moral judgments and personality tests explained by gender, and detecting explicit gender attribute mention rates in open-ended self-introductions.

Measuring the proportion of behavioral variance in moral judgments and personality tests explained by political ideology, and calculating explicit political affiliation mention rates in open-ended self-introductions.

Measuring the proportion of behavioral variance in moral judgments and personality tests explained by the persona's country of residence, and evaluating explicit country mention rates in open-ended self-introductions.

Measuring the proportion of behavioral variance in moral judgments and personality tests explained by social class, and calculating how often socioeconomic descriptors are explicitly mentioned or systematically truncated in open-ended self-introductions.
Measuring the proportion of behavioral variance in moral judgments and personality tests explained by age, and detecting age-related keyword mention rates in open-ended self-introductions.

Qualitative analysis of model refusals when prompted to generate self-introductions for personas with intellectual disabilities, highlighting implicit coherence priors and tensions between safety alignment and stereotyping.
